younger.one_minute: Russia and Ukraine are at war, and Russian forces hold about a fifth of Ukraine. Lately both sides have been attacking each other's power plants and oil sites from far away. On 11 October, US President Trump said they had agreed to stop hitting energy sites, but the attacks did not stop.

who.name: Russia
who.about: Its forces hold about a fifth of Ukraine.

who.name: The United States
who.about: President Trump announced the pause on hitting energy sites.

questions.a: A promise to stop attacking power plants, power lines and oil refineries, even if other fighting goes on.
Not yet. Ukraine says Russia kept hitting its power sites, and Russia's foreign minister said no to it.

questions.q: Why did the lights go out in Ukraine?
questions.a: Strikes on power sites left at least 600,000 people without electricity, Ukraine's president said.

younger.worry: It's okay to feel worried when you read about war. Leaders in many countries are talking about how to make the fighting stop. If something you read upsets you, tell a grown-up you trust. Talking about it helps.

older.one_minute: Russia's war in Ukraine is increasingly fought from the air: the armies are largely deadlocked on the ground, and about a fifth of Ukraine is under Russian occupation. On 11 October President Trump announced an "energy ceasefire". Ukraine said it would comply if Russia did; Russia's foreign minister rejected it, and Russian strikes on Ukraine's power system went on, cutting electricity to 600,000 people.

who.name: Volodymyr Zelenskyy
who.about: Ukraine's president; backs an energy truce if Russia complies.

who.name: Vladimir Putin
who.about: Russia's president; US envoys say he is not ready to negotiate an end.

who.name: Sergey Lavrov
who.about: Russia's foreign minister; rejected the energy pause.

who.name: Donald Trump
who.about: US president; announced the pause and eased sanctions on Russian diesel.

who.name: The EU
who.about: Approved its largest set of sanctions on Russia since 2022.

questions.a: Each side has been striking the other's energy system: Russia hits Ukraine's power plants and grid, and Ukraine hits Russian oil refineries with long-range drones.

Two days before the announcement, the US eased sanctions so Russia could supply it with diesel. Ukrainian and European officials said this helps fund Russia's war, and US senators from both parties objected.
Ukraine's constitution bars elections under martial law, in force since February 2022. Mr Zelenskyy says he would organise one if Russia agreed to a 60-day full ceasefire.

older.worry: News of war can feel heavy. Diplomats are still talking: Ukraine says it would accept an energy truce if Russia does, and the Kremlin says contacts are continuing. If the news is upsetting you, it's fine to take a break from it and talk to someone you trust.

timeline.younger: Ukraine began living under special wartime rules because of the war with Russia.
timeline.older: Ukraine comes under martial law, still in force, during the war with Russia.

timeline.younger: The US agreed a deal for Russia to supply it with diesel fuel.
timeline.older: The US eases sanctions so Russia can supply it with diesel; Ukrainian and European officials criticise the deal.

timeline.younger: President Trump said Russia and Ukraine had agreed to stop attacking energy sites.
timeline.older: Mr Trump announces an "energy ceasefire", effective immediately. Neither Moscow nor Kyiv confirms it.

timeline.younger: Ukraine said Russia was still attacking its power sites. Russia's foreign minister said no to the pause.
timeline.older: Ukraine reports fresh strikes on energy sites, including a power plant in Kharkiv; Foreign Minister Lavrov rejects the idea.

timeline.younger: Strikes left at least 600,000 people in Ukraine without electricity.
timeline.older: Overnight strikes leave at least 600,000 Ukrainians without power; the EU approves its largest sanctions package since 2022.

timeline.younger: Russia hit power plants again. Ukraine said it would start hitting Russian oil sites again.
timeline.older: Russian strikes kill at least nine and cut power to over half a million; on 15 October Zelenskyy says Kyiv is done with the energy pause and refinery strikes will resume.

timeline.younger: European leaders said they would keep backing Ukraine. Ukraine's president asked for more money.
timeline.older: At a Brussels summit EU leaders keep sanctions on Russia; Zelenskyy asks for an extra 70 billion euros for next year and the Commission is asked how to fill the gap.

timeline.younger: Ukraine sent more than 1,000 drones at Russia, and an oil port in St Petersburg caught fire. Russia hit Kyiv overnight.
timeline.older: Ukraine launches more than 1,000 drones at Russia, setting an oil terminal and depot ablaze in St Petersburg; Russia says it destroyed 1,015. A Russian strike kills a woman in Kyiv.

timeline.younger: A US envoy met Ukraine's leader in Norway, and the US president asked him to make a deal.
timeline.older: Witkoff meets Zelenskyy and European leaders in Oslo; at the White House Trump presses Zelenskyy to make a deal with Russia, saying the US has got “absolutely nothing back” from Ukraine.

timeline.younger: Russia's leader met a US envoy. A Russian adviser said Putin agreed to restart three-way talks after 10 November.
timeline.older: Putin meets US envoy Witkoff in St Petersburg; the Kremlin says he agreed in principle to resume three-way talks with the US and Ukraine after 10 November.

timeline.younger: Ukraine's leader said Ukraine, Russia and the US agreed to hold three-way talks next month.
timeline.older: Zelenskyy says Ukraine, Russia and the US have agreed to trilateral talks next month and renews his call to meet Putin on territory; Russia says it will not halt hostilities during the talks.
